title: Twice a year at Amritsar
hookLine: the misls met as the Sarbat Khalsa at Vaisakhi and Diwali to decide together before the Granth

lines: RIVALS, EACH WITH HIS OWN RIDERS.
cards: Who decides, when nobody is king? The misl chiefs argued over villages, grazing and who owed whom; some had fought each other. No ruler stood over them, and each answered to his own riders.
Yet at Vaisakhi in spring and Diwali in autumn, Sikh histories say, they came to Amritsar, sat down together, and put the Guru Granth Sahib in front of them.

teach.b: The gathering had a name: the Sarbat Khalsa. Sarbat means all, the whole: not one chief's council, not a king's court. In principle, every band had a place in it.

teach.h: SEATED BEFORE THE GURU GRANTH SAHIB.
teach.b: Tradition says the assembly met before the Guru Granth Sahib, near the Akal Takht. The scripture wasn't decoration; it was the presence they decided in front of.
A chief who might shout in his own camp had to speak here as one Sikh among others before the Guru. Then what came out of it.
A decision reached this way was called a gurmata, which Sikhs describe as a resolution of the Guru, made by the gathered Khalsa in the Guru's presence. Once agreed, it bound the bands together.
Sikh histories say this is how the misls chose shared leaders, planned joint campaigns, and set their quarrels aside, at least for a season. And notice the season.
Vaisakhi and Diwali were already festival days, when people came to Amritsar anyway to bathe in the pool and see the Harmandir.
The meeting rode on the back of the celebration: faith first, then business, and the business done in faith's presence. A people with no single ruler found a single voice, twice a year.

how: Sikhs still speak of the Sarbat Khalsa and the gurmata, and Sikh congregations take decisions before the Guru Granth Sahib, often ending with Ardas.

games.q: you're a misl chief at Amritsar for Diwali. a rival chief is in the same gathering. a joint decision has to be made. how is it done?
o: the whole Khalsa agrees it before the Guru Granth Sahib.
games.why: the Sarbat Khalsa agreed a gurmata in the Guru's presence, and it bound every band, rivals included.

practice: Bring to mind one choice that isn't yours alone, with a partner, a family, a team, and notice how you usually make it: decide and announce, or wait for someone else?
Then picture sitting down with them in a quiet room, nobody shouting, something larger than all of you present, and hear what you'd say differently. If you pray, rest in Waheguru on each breath out.

wordCard.voice: gurmata, a resolution agreed by the whole Khalsa before the Guru Granth Sahib, at the gatherings held twice a year at Amritsar, at Vaisakhi and Diwali, as the Sarbat Khalsa. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: gurmata, a resolution of the gathered Khalsa made before the Guru.

carryVoice: Your line: decide before the guru. One voice, from many bands. Nine hundred days, and still going.
